## Research Question

Can attributes of an athlete help explain Olympic medal success?

## Load Data

```{r load-data}
# Load the package and the complete dataset
library(olympicAthletes)
data(olympic_athletes)

athletes_raw <- olympic_athletes

data.frame(
  rows = nrow(athletes_raw),
  columns = ncol(athletes_raw)
)
```

## Remove Missing Athlete Attributes

```{r remove-missing}
# Remove rows missing sex, age, height, or weight
athletes_clean <- athletes_raw[
  complete.cases(athletes_raw[, c("sex", "age", "height", "weight")]),
]

# Report how many rows were removed
data.frame(
  before = nrow(athletes_raw),
  after = nrow(athletes_clean),
  removed = nrow(athletes_raw) - nrow(athletes_clean)
)
```

## Remove Duplicate Rows

```{r remove-duplicates}
# Remove completely identical rows
rows_before <- nrow(athletes_clean)

athletes_clean <- athletes_clean[
  !duplicated(athletes_clean),
]

# Report how many duplicates were removed
data.frame(
  before = rows_before,
  after = nrow(athletes_clean),
  removed = rows_before - nrow(athletes_clean)
)
```

## Identify Medal Success

```{r medal-success}
# Mark medal-winning participations: 1 = medal, 0 = no medal
athletes_clean$medal_won <- as.integer(
  !is.na(athletes_clean$medal)
)

# Count participations with and without a medal
data.frame(
  outcome = c("No medal", "Medal"),
  participations = c(
    sum(athletes_clean$medal_won == 0),
    sum(athletes_clean$medal_won == 1)
  )
)
```

## Inspect Numeric Values

```{r inspect-values}
# Summarize age, height in cm, and weight in kg
summary(athletes_clean[, c("age", "height", "weight")])
```

## Inspect Extreme Records

```{r inspect-extremes}
# Identify minimum and maximum values without removing them
extreme_rows <- subset(
  athletes_clean,
  age %in% range(age) |
    height %in% range(height) |
    weight %in% range(weight)
)

# Display the extreme records with their sporting context
extreme_rows[, c(
  "name", "sex", "age", "height", "weight",
  "sport", "event", "year", "medal"
)]
```
